title: `notifications/message`
description: Structured server log records at RFC 5424 levels, enabled per request through a log level in that request's `_meta`.
question: Can a developer see the server's own logs through the framework?
why: This is the only channel through which a server explains itself while a call is in flight, and it is the difference between debugging a failing integration and guessing at it. Note that the connection-wide `logging/setLevel` was removed in this revision: log level is now per request, so a framework that sets it once at startup gets nothing.
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.

notes.crewai: CrewAI 1.15.26: mcpadapt builds its `ClientSession` without a `logging_callback`. The server's `notifications/message` arrive, and the SDK's default handler drops them before any caller sees them.
notes.genkit_js: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: server log messages are delivered only to a `LoggingMessageNotificationSchema` handler set on the SDK client; @genkit-ai/mcp has no API for it and registers no notification handler; it works only on the SDK `Client` that the public getter `GenkitMcpClient.mcpClient` hands out (route `session`).
notes.google_adk: Google ADK 2.11.0: `McpToolset` has no logging hook, and the `ClientSession` its `MCPSessionManager` builds is given no `logging_callback`. The server's `notifications/message` arrive, and the SDK's default handler drops them before any caller sees them.
notes.autogen: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench` opens its `ClientSession` without a `logging_callback`; the server's `notifications/message` reach no caller.
notes.strands: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `MCPClient` opens its `ClientSession` with its own `message_handler` and no `logging_callback`, and takes no log hook, so the server's `notifications/message` never reach the caller.
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): MCPClient registers no notification handler: a server notification reaches only `onUncaughtError`, as an "Unsupported message type" error that does not name the notification. The server's five `notifications/message` never reach the caller, and there is no logging option on `createMCPClient`.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the server options take no message or logging handler. The server sent `notifications/message` and nothing in the SDK received it.
notes.llamaindex: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `BasicMCPClient` builds its `ClientSession` without a `logging_callback`. The server's `notifications/message` arrive and the SDK's default handler drops them. `tool_call_logs_callback` collects Python `logging` records from the client process, not MCP log notifications.
notes.google_adk_js: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: reachable only on a raw `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` `Client` from `MCPSessionManager.createSession()`, a public export of `@google/adk/tools/mcp`, with `setNotificationHandler(LoggingMessageNotificationSchema)`. The sessions `MCPToolset` opens register no handler, so an agent never sees `notifications/message`.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` takes no log handler; its fastmcp `Client` uses fastmcp's default, which writes server log messages to Python logging, so none reaches the agent or caller.
notes.haystack: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPClient` builds its `ClientSession` without a `logging_callback` and `MCPToolset` takes no log handler, so the server's five `notifications/message` reached the caller as nothing.
notes.smolagents: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): mcpadapt builds its `ClientSession` without a `logging_callback`. The server's `notifications/message` arrive, and the SDK's default handler drops them before any caller sees them.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy takes no log handler. Server log messages reach a caller only through a `logging_callback` on the caller's own `mcp.Client`, which DSPy is handed by `Tool.from_mcp_tool` and never configures. DSPy itself offers no route.
notes.spring_ai: Spring AI 2.0.1: the server's five `notifications/message` arrive on the wire, but MCP Java SDK 2.0.0 types `LoggingMessageNotification.data` as a String. Structured data such as `{"message": ...}` fails to deserialize (`Cannot deserialize value of type java.lang.String from Object value`), `McpClientSession` logs `Error handling notification`, and `@McpLogging` receives none of them.
notes.beeai: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: no logging hook. Log messages reach the caller only on a `ClientSession` the caller builds and hands `MCPTool.from_client`, which BeeAI uses as given; the session BeeAI opens itself for a transport has no callbacks, via `logging_callback`.
notes.copilot_sdk: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): the runtime receives the server's `notifications/message` (5 on the wire) but surfaces none of them: no session event fires, and `session.rpc.diagnostics.read` holds only the server's stderr. The caller received 0.
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient.connect` builds its `ClientSession` from the transport streams alone, with no `logging_callback`, and `MCPServerStdio`/`MCPServerHTTP`/`MCPServerSSE` take no hook for it, so the server's `notifications/message` reach nothing.
notes.google_adk_java: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: MCP Java SDK mcp-core 2.0.0 types `LoggingMessageNotification.data` as `String`, so a log notification with object data fails to deserialize (`Cannot deserialize value of type java.lang.String from Object value`); `McpClientSession` logs `Error handling notification` and drops it. The server sent 5 `notifications/message` and the `McpServerLogConsumer` that `McpSessionManager` installs received 0.
notes.koog: Koog 1.3.0-beta: Koog registers no logging handler. `Client.setNotificationHandler(notifications/message)` on the Kotlin SDK `Client` handed to `fromClient` received all 5 messages.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): mcptoolset has no logging option. A `mcp.ClientOptions.LoggingMessageHandler` on the `*mcp.Client` the caller passes as `mcptoolset.Config.Client` receives all five `notifications/message`, but only by configuring go-sdk rather than the toolset.
